userFeedback: 战士和弓箭手打击需要金属碰撞感；保留重量、短弓风，火雷沿用当前版本。
production: Original deterministic modelling using installed NumPy/SciPy/FFmpeg; no recordings, AI calls, downloaded samples or new dependencies.
runtimeIntegration: Offline audition only; no game runtime audio or former study files changed.
listeningAcceptance: Pending judgement of blade/arrowhead metal identity and weight; numerical measures are not perceptual acceptance.

war.userPreference: 2026-11-16: sword and arrow impacts should have metal-collision identity; retain v6 weight and short bow air, without returning to sharp thin pings.
war.provenance: Original deterministic NumPy/SciPy material modelling added to the v6 source. No recordings, downloads, AI calls, external samples or listening acceptance claimed.
war.body: The existing thick v6 sword/body waveform is retained as the foundation, at its original gain before the common safety ceiling.
war.steelStructure: A 1.3ms irregular mechanical excitation and a small trailing contact fold drive separate non-harmonic modes near 700/1100/1700/2400Hz. Modal decay is 36-64ms with shorter high-mode damping; the result is a contact clank rather than continuous high noise.
war.materialDifference: Soft contact uses a light blade resonance and small scrape. Armor has more independent plate motion and a clearer short scrape. Finish sits between them. Swing remains unchanged with no manufactured hit.
war.spectralBalance: New energy is concentrated in the 650-2600Hz material band while the accepted 180-700Hz body remains. Modes and exciter are changed, not the overall pitch or a global treble/gain control.
war.tail: Steel response is finite, with no room reverb or long ringing bell; v6 dark aftermotion remains subordinate.
war.mix: Local active-window RMS assigns contact-layer energy; a final .64 ceiling is protection only. Three variants alter excitation, contact spacing, modal damping and frequency jitter.
war.comparisonApi: synth_contact(variation=1,material="soft"|"armor",sample_rate=44100) maps to the same war_slash/war_armor sources used in demonstrations.
war.acceptance: Spectrum and decay checks describe the source changes; human and device listening remain pending.

bow.userPreference: Give warrior/bow impacts metal collision character while retaining the previously requested weight and short bow air.
bow.provenance: Original deterministic NumPy/SciPy material models using the accepted v6 bow source. No recordings, soundbanks, downloads, AI or playback.
bow.unchangedPreparation: bow_draw and bow_release directly reuse v6; no late air wake, guitar-like pluck or new pitched string is introduced.
bow.arrowMetal: A finite noise excitation drives localized non-harmonic 947/1361/1987/2719Hz tip modes. They damp in roughly 10–30ms and finish within 0.12s, with a small retouch rather than a long ringing plate.
bow.body: The v6 puncture, shaft recoil and weighted low-mid body are retained. Armor adds a small 251/443/719Hz contact support beneath the tip resonance.

materialPolicy.synth_cue.bow_pierce: Subtle arrowhead resonance; this does not assert that every target wears armor.
materialPolicy.synth_cue.bow_heavy: Firmer local contact and very short metal rebound, still below a full armored collision.
materialPolicy.synth_contact.soft: Ordinary weighted v6 puncture; no added armor clang.
materialPolicy.synth_contact.armor: A distinctly harder localized metal contact over the same puncture, for an armored target.

bow.air: No new air source. Existing v6 release/pierce/heavy air ends by .083/.064/.074s.
bow.mix: Source peak cap .64 is safety only; target material changes source layers rather than uniformly raising playback gain.
bow.acceptance: Finite samples and envelope/frequency measures are technical evidence; metal identity and preference need user audition.

designNotes.performance: Same V6 event onsets/gains. One basic arrow is explicitly an armour demonstration; ordinary contacts have quieter metal identity.
designNotes.elemental: 18 source clips and 2 complete solo demos/cue sets are byte-identical copies of V6.

comparison.reference: PCM WAV; MP3 is a convenience preview.
